title: Seven years, 34 moments
lede: From incorporation to the final filing, with the market and the rivals alongside. Filter by thread.

events.title: Incorporated
events.text: Pets.com, Inc. is incorporated in California.

events.title: Operations begin
events.text: Buys the Pets.com domain and web store from a third party. The founding-era site described itself as “a division of WebMagic™”.

events.title: Julie Wainwright named CEO
events.text: The former Reel.com chief executive joins as CEO and director. Chris Deyo follows as president in April.

events.title: $10.0M Series A and an Amazon ad deal
events.text: 5,781,862 Series A preferred shares. An advertising agreement with Amazon.com is dated Apr 22.

events.title: PetSmart and Idealab form PetSmart.com
events.text: A 50/50 joint venture in Pasadena. Each parent contributes $10M in cash.

events.title: $50.0M Series B
events.text: Amazon becomes the largest shareholder.

events.title: Union City distribution center
events.text: Sublease of 143,232 sq ft at 33201 Dowe Ave. Web store version 2 launches in July.

events.title: Petopia raises $66M
events.text: The Petco-backed rival closes a large round.

events.title: PetSmart.com raises $50M+
events.text: A second round for the PetSmart/Idealab venture.

events.title: Petstore.com raises $97M
events.text: Discovery Communications becomes its largest shareholder.

events.title: Macy’s parade balloon
events.text: A sock-puppet balloon flies in the Thanksgiving Day Parade.

events.title: Indiana DC leased; S-1 filed
events.text: A distribution center in Greenwood, near Indianapolis, is leased Dec 7. Another $49.2M of preferred stock is raised in Nov–Dec, and the S-1 is filed.

events.title: Petopia adds $35M
events.text: Total funding is reported at about $114M.

events.title: Disney/ABC airtime for stock
events.text: 1,378,000 Series C shares are issued for ABC network media time valued at $11.02M.

events.title: Super Bowl XXXIV ad
events.text: The sock puppet gets its own spot on ABC, widely reported at about $1.2M (secondary source).

events.title: PetSmart.com files a $115M IPO
events.text: The stock market is still open to e-tailers.

events.title: IPO at $11
events.text: 7.5M shares on Nasdaq as IPET: $82.5M gross, about $75.3M net.

events.title: The Nasdaq peaks
events.text: It closes at 5,048.62, its bubble high. By year-end it is 2,470.52.

events.title: $20 sock puppets ship
events.text: Slate calls it “The Puppet That Ate a Dot-Com.”

events.title: Buys Petstore.com
events.text: All stock: 5.8M common shares plus preferred stock. It brings in $3M of cash.

events.title: $23.1M cash left
events.text: Cumulative net loss: $146.6M. Merrill Lynch is shopping the company.

events.title: Petopia lays off most staff
events.text: About 60% of employees are cut.

events.title: Wind-down announced
events.text: About 255 of 320 staff are laid off and IPET closes at $0.22. “No party was prepared to provide capital or acquire the company.”

events.title: The store closes
events.text: “We have closed our virtual doors.” Orders placed before 11am PT ship.

events.title: PetSmart.com pulls its IPO
events.text: PetSmart later raises its stake to 81%.

events.title: Petco buys Petopia’s assets
events.text: Petopia cancels its planned IPO in Feb 2001.

events.title: Domain sold to PetSmart.com
events.text: $375,000 for the domain names and IP. The sock puppet is excluded.

events.title: Proxy: “up to approximately $0.25”
events.text: The board asks stockholders to approve dissolution.

events.title: Dissolved and delisted
events.text: Renamed IPET Holdings. Last close: $0.125. The remaining staff resign.

events.title: Payout #1: $0.09
events.text: Initial liquidating distribution.

events.title: Puppet joins 1-800-BarNone
events.text: The rights were bought for $125,000. New slogan: “Everyone deserves a second chance.”

events.title: Payout #2: $0.075
events.text: Second liquidating distribution.

events.title: Final payout: $0.00747
events.text: The shares are declared worthless.

events.title: Registration ends
events.text: Form 15 filed. The company leaves the public record.
